# broken-pipeline-lab

A deliberately broken CI/CD test fixture. Each workflow fails in a different,
realistic way, so the Autonomous DevOps Pipeline Agent has varied ground-truth
failures to detect, parse, diagnose, and recommend fixes for.

## Failure scenarios

| # | Workflow file | Trigger path | Failure type | Expected root cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `01-missing-dependency.yml` | `ap

p/main.py`, `requirements.txt` | `ModuleNotFoundError` | `requests` is imported but missing from `requirements.txt` |
| 2 | `02-failing-tests.yml` | `tests/**` | `AssertionError` | `test_add_is_correct` asserts the wrong expected value |
| 3 | `03-docker-build-fail.yml` | `Dockerfile` | Docker build error | `COPY main.py .` references a path that doesn't exist (`app/main.py` is the real path) |
|

4 | `04-invalid-yaml.yml` | itself | Workflow parse failure | Bad indentation + duplicate `run:` key — YAML never parses, job never starts |
| 5 | `05-syntax-error.yml` | `app/broken_syntax.py` | `SyntaxError` | Missing colon in function definition |

## Why these five

They're chosen to be maximally distinct at every stage of the pipeline your
agents will process:

- **1 & 5** both crash at "run

script" but need different fixes (edit a
  manifest file vs. edit source code) — good test that Root Cause Analysis
  doesn't just pattern-match on "Python error."
- **2** fails *after* a clean install and clean parse — tests that Log
  Analysis can find the real error inside a wall of pytest output, not just
  the first traceback it sees.
- **3** never touches Python tooling at all — tests that y

our agents
  generalize beyond Python-specific log formats.
- **4** never even starts a job (GitHub Actions rejects the workflow file
  itself) — tests that your Monitoring Agent can detect and label failures
  that have no logs to download at all. This is an edge case a lot of
  first-pass implementations miss.

## How to use this repo

1. Push this repo to GitHub (see steps below).
2. Push a sma

ll change to trigger one workflow at a time — e.g. edit
   `app/main.py` and commit, which fires scenario 1 (edit only files listed
   in that workflow's `paths:` so you trigger scenarios one at a time
   instead of all five firing on every push).
3. Confirm in the **Actions** tab that the run failed and inspect the raw
   logs — this is exactly what your CI Monitoring Agent will fetch via the

GitHub API in Phase 3.
4. Once your agents exist, point them at this repo as their target and
   compare their diagnosis/fix output against the "expected root cause"
   column above — that's your evaluation set.

## Pushing to GitHub

```bash
cd broken-pipeline-lab
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial broken pipeline lab"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/<your-usern

ame>/broken-pipeline-lab.git
git push -u origin main
```

After the push, go to the **Actions** tab on GitHub and enable workflows if
prompted. Trigger any workflow manually via `workflow_dispatch` (the "Run
workflow" button) if you don't want to wait for a matching path change.
